sections.html:
McClain County sits in south central Oklahoma, inside the Oklahoma City metro area, and its county seat is Purcell. The 2020 Census counted 41,662 residents and 16,421 housing units. About 79.8 percent of occupied homes are owner occupied and 7.2 percent of all units were vacant, so most sales here are ordinary family homes.

The cities are Blanchard, Newcastle and Purcell. Towns include Byars, Cole, Dibble, Goldsby, Maysville, Rosedale, Washington and Wayne. Each parcel's bill is built from the county, the city or town it sits in, and its school district. Full K-12 districts here include Alex, Asher, Blanchard, Bridge Creek, Dibble, Lindsay, Maysville, Newcastle, Norman, Paoli, Purcell, Stratford, Washington and Wayne, and each one levies its own tax. Two houses of equal value in different districts can carry different bills.

Interstate 35 is the busiest road, and buyers tend to ask about commute time before anything else.

Two elected offices split the work. The County Assessor values property and prepares the tax roll. The County Treasurer collects the money and passes it on to the county, cities, towns and schools. Both offices are in the courthouse annex in Purcell.

You can search the tax roll and pay online at oktaxrolls.com. The assessor also keeps records and maps, runs a four-year visual inspection program, takes exemption applications and sits on the board that corrects the tax roll. The McClain County Assessor page and the treasurer page have the current details.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
The assessor sets the value, the Excise Board certifies the millage, and the treasurer sends the bill. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value. Assessment ratios in Oklahoma run between 10 and 15 percent, and mill rates commonly fall between 90 and 110.

Every local government sets its own levy, and a property's total rate adds up the county, the city or town and the school district. A house in Newcastle and one in Wayne can land in different school districts and see different totals.

  • Value comes from the assessor, who inspects each real property on a four-year cycle.
  • Levies come from the taxing bodies and are certified by the Excise Board.
  • The treasurer mails the bill once the assessor files the finished roll.

The first installment is not delinquent until 30 days after the assessor files the completed rolls with the treasurer.

Property tax is payable November 1 under the statewide schedule. Pay at least half before January 1 and the rest before April 1. If half is not paid before January 1, the whole levy turns delinquent.

  • Balances of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1.
  • Late tax accrues 1.5 percent interest per month, capped at the amount of the unpaid tax.
  • Mortgage servicers pay one annual payment before January 1.
  • The treasurer may waive penalty or interest that came through no fault of the taxpayer.

If you plan to close between November and March, find out whether the first half has been paid. A delinquent account is handled differently from one that is current, and the title company will want the answer early.

Start with a written protest to the assessor. After a notice of increased valuation, you have 30 calendar days from the mailing date. If your value did not change, the protest is due by the first Monday in April.

The assessor holds an informal hearing and must send a written decision within 7 calendar days. If you disagree, you have 15 calendar days from the mailing date of that decision to appeal to the county board of equalization. File the protest form with the required valuation information, because without it the assessor's number is presumed correct on appeal.

Bring comparable sales, repair estimates and photos of any damage. A short, documented protest usually gets a better hearing than a general complaint.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the 3 percent cap
sections.html:
A primary home gets a $1,000 homestead exemption off taxable value, and its assessed value cannot grow more than 3 percent a year unless it sells. Homestead applications go to the assessor, not the treasurer.

A sale resets that cap. A buyer's first bill can look higher than yours, which is worth mentioning to a buyer who plans around the seller's number. The exemption belongs to the owner who lives in the home, so a buyer files their own application after the deed is recorded.

Unpaid property tax is settled out of sale proceeds at closing, and the title company asks the treasurer for a payoff. City charges for weeds, cleanup, paving or nuisance abatement are certified to the treasurer once delinquent and sit as a lien on the parcel, so ask about those too.

The treasurer also manages county-owned property acquired at annual delinquent-tax sales, so a parcel left unpaid long enough can leave the owner's hands. If you are behind or inherited a house with back taxes, get the real payoff number first.

  1. Look up the parcel on oktaxrolls.com and note every year with a balance.
  2. Call the treasurer for a written payoff that includes interest.
  3. Ask the city about any certified weed or cleanup charges.
  4. Give the figures to the title company so the closing statement is clear.

The usual situations are inherited homes, houses with deferred repairs, rentals with tenants in place and parcels with back taxes. Roughly one in five occupied homes in the county is rented.

A fast cash sale suits owners who want to skip showings, inspection negotiations and a lender's repair list. Rural parcels near the Canadian and Washita rivers, hilly lots in the west and older homes in Purcell and Byars each raise different repair questions, and selling as-is means you do not fix them first. Whichever route you take, get a written payoff of taxes and any city liens before choosing, so the net figure is clear.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a McClain County valuation?
faqs.a: The County Assessor handles values. The office is at 121 N. 2nd Ave, Room 206 in Purcell, phone 405-527-3520.

faqs.q: When are McClain County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are payable November 1. At least half must be paid before January 1 or the full levy becomes delinquent, and the second half is due before April 1.

faqs.q: How much interest does a late bill collect?
faqs.a: Delinquent Oklahoma property tax collects 1.5 percent interest per month, and interest stops growing once it equals the unpaid tax.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest a valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the mailing date of an increase notice, or until the first Monday in April if the value did not change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McClain County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is paid from proceeds at closing, and the treasurer's office can supply the payoff amount.
